modules.name: Vista audit and node contract
modules.design_question: Which Vista parts become the View-and-Warn node, and what typed ports does it expose to the rest of the platform?
modules.method: Vista v09.16 is one WebGL2 page: explorer.js (218 KB, 161 functions, one global state), report.js, pdf.js, six self-test scripts. KEEP: polygon-clip overlap kernels, result precedence and no-compliance wording guards, fixtures F1-F3, hash state, PDF writer, cone-fit camera rule. REFACTOR: split explorer.js into assets, picking, camera and ui modules; replace the global state and the /api/check shim with typed functions; run checks in a Worker; port self-tests to a headless runner. REPLACE: the 38.7 MB triangle context, apex-only origins, the flat ceiling as main test, per-part bounding-box checks, the duplicate cone copy in Form Studio and the equirectangular frame of Vista (x = dlon*111320*cos(lat0), y = dlat*110574). Against a GRS80 geodesic that frame is 0.20% short east-west, 0.58% short north-south, up to 0.118 deg off in azimuth, and 25.7 m short on the 4.59 km QE-to-Barclay line. Kernels therefore run in a metric frame (EPSG:3157 or per-cone ENU) with horizontal datum and epoch recorded. Every output carries units, CRS, vertical datum, dataset versions and an estimate flag. Vertical datum may be UNKNOWN: viewing works, exceedance numbers are blocked and the card says relative only. Add MIT or Apache licence files; keep the ODbL notice on OSM-derived tiles.

modules.name: Protected-viewpoint camera rig
modules.design_question: How do we render the design from each protected origin with correct position, eye height and a field of view matched to the cone?
modules.method: Origin: City survey coordinates and geodetic elevation when obtained (quality Q2); otherwise the polygon apex (Q0, labelled estimated; the four QE apexes agree within 0.33 m). Open-data text for 9.1 and 9.2 names the Walking Figures plaza but the 2026 Table 1 extract names the City Hall stairs, so those apexes may lag. Eye z = ground z + eye height (default 1.6 m, editable; City value not found). Ground z comes from the LiDAR-2022 DTM (0.081 m at 95% on open ground); piers, bridges and seawalls (G1, G2, E, K) use first returns plus a structure offset. Heading = bisector of the two boundary azimuths. Presets: cone-fit (Vista rule hfov = clamp(1.5 x spread + 8, 24, 100 deg); pitch toward the limit-plane footprint plus margin) and standard 39.6 deg. The camera record stores hfov, vfov and aspect; the interactive view (vertical 60 deg default) and the PDF share one preset function. Depth: reversed-Z (three.js reversedDepthBuffer, needs EXT_clip_control) or a logarithmic buffer, near 1-2 m, far at least 60 km, because named subjects lie 12.5-24.6 km away. Overlay the boundaries, the limit-plane footprint and a quality badge. Calibrate each view once against a site photo (landmarks within 0.3 deg).

modules.design_question: How do we offer trustworthy views from nearby roofs and rank which ones matter?
modules.method: Vista picks the highest modelled roof triangle (normal Z share at least 0.35), prefers high, broad, central surfaces, lists up to six buildings within 600 m and sets the eye 1.6 m above the roof; its roof heights are OSM-derived and unverified. Upgrade: (1) roof z from LiDAR-2022 first returns and building-class points per footprint (CGVD28, 0.081 m at 95% on open ground), shown beside OSM height plus LiDAR ground, footprints-2009 topelev_m (2009, stale) and, outside the City, HRDEM DSM (CGVD2013, about +0.15 m preliminary shift); spread = max minus min; (2) OSM height excludes antennas and spires, so flag appurtenances; (3) rank candidates by elevation angle to the design top, distance, unobstructed ray (BVH) and whether the roof lies inside any cone; (4) a grid index replaces whole-city scans; (5) access stays unknown unless a public viewing roof is listed; (6) never imply a rooftop is an official viewpoint. Output RooftopViewpoint with source, roof z plus or minus spread and building id. Reuse the Vista rooftop self-test (stable building ids restored from the URL hash).

modules.name: Cone limit estimate and violation warning
modules.design_question: How do we estimate each cone limit at any point and warn which cone, by how many metres, where, citing the clause and saying it is an estimate?
modules.method: The Guidelines (s.2, p.3) define a cone as two vertical boundaries plus a horizontal lower boundary that sets the maximum geodetic height; the 2024 Council report (RTS 16338, Appendix B Table 2) aligns each lower boundary with the roof of a named reference building. Polygons give plan extent only. Default H0: constant limit L per cone or sub-cone. H1, the 1995-99 City sheet L = Lv + (Lr-Lv) Dx/Dr (slope about 2.05-2.12 deg for old View 9.1), stays a competing historical model; fit both, allow s = 0. Tiers: T0 user ceiling; T1a published site-vertex limits from at least 2 sites spanning at least 30% of the cone length, dated after 2024-07-10 or for cones absent from Table 2; T1b L = LiDAR-2022 roof z of the reference building, tested against T1a rows; T2 City data. Test by polygon clipping in the metric frame; e = z_top - L(P). Governing limit = minimum over covering cones; zoning or ODP height may be lower. States: outside, near edge (inside the plan buffer, tested as inside), clear, within uncertainty, above. Print estimate; cite the clause numbered 3.1.1 (p.6, printed under heading 3.2); list 3.1.2-3.1.5, 3.3, 3.4 as human review.

modules.name: Skyline comparison and PDF report
modules.design_question: How do we show what the design changes in the existing view and export it as evidence?
modules.method: Render Existing and Proposed from one camera with a wipe slider. Skyline profile: for each azimuth (step 0.1 deg; 0.05 deg for cones narrower than 5 deg) across the cone plus 2 deg each side, march outward over a heightfield (LiDAR DTM, LOD1 roofs, design) and keep the maximum elevation angle; or read the top pixel of each image column. Apply d^2 (1-k)/(2R) with k = 0.13 to the skyline only, never to the City limit. Rays = (spread + 4 deg)/step: the 1.61 deg cone needs 56 at 0.1 deg or 112 at 0.05; the 53 deg cone 570 or 1,140. Outputs: three angle arrays, skyline area added (deg^2), share of cone width where the design rises above the existing skyline, margin to the estimated limit line. Keep the Vista report engine and add the vector profile chart, violation table with plus or minus U, datum line, tier, estimate stamp and a provenance appendix with dataset dates and hashes. Existing context must share an epoch: print LiDAR 2022-09, OSM access date and studio-model date on each image. Add alt text, non-colour cues (WCAG 1.4.1) and a live status region (WCAG 4.1.3).

modules.name: Design ingest and georeferencing
modules.design_question: How do .3dm, OBJ and IFC models become a placed, mesh-level DesignMassing with an explicit datum?
modules.method: Vista reads .3dm in the browser with rhino3dm (WebAssembly, MIT): meshes, extrusions and brep render meshes, a unit table (mm to yards), caps of 80 MB and 2 M triangles; OBJ is parsed locally; placement puts the model bounding-box base on the terrain at the site; the cone check uses one bounding box per part, which can overestimate. New contract DesignMassing {parts[id, layer, positions Float32, indices Uint32], units, source SHA-256, placement{anchor lat/lon, rotation, base z, datum}}. Placement modes: on site (as Vista), with base z from the LiDAR-2022 DTM and its sigma shown; or as-modelled coordinates with declared EPSG (EPSG:3157 for Vancouver) and vertical datum. Vertical datum may be UNKNOWN: the model can be viewed but exceedance numbers are blocked. Layers named mechanical, antenna or mast are flagged as appurtenances, which clause 3.1.1 includes. IFC through web-ifc; breps without render meshes are reported, never silently dropped. Test: the triangle check equals the bounding-box check on boxes and is lower on a stepped tower. Everything stays on the device; nothing is uploaded.

modules.design_question: What size and compute budget keeps the node usable on a student laptop and on GitHub Pages?
modules.method: Baseline from the files: the Vista pack is 38.7 MB with 1.09 M building triangles, and roof, terrain and pick queries scan triangles linearly. At the GitHub Pages soft 100 GB per month, 38.7 MB per cold load allows about 2,600 loads; 3 MB allows about 33,000. Targets: under 5 MB to first interaction, under 20 MB total, 30 fps on integrated graphics, under 500 MB tab memory. Moves: (1) build offline from lidar-2022 (1 km LAS zips, 16.45 MB to 2.74 GB each; the 17 origins fall in 11 tiles, downtown needs about 16): derive DTM and roof heights and publish only int16 decimetre heightfields (1 m within 100 m of each origin, 4-5 m city-wide, 25-50 m North Shore backdrop from HRDEM); (2) LOD1 int16 rings (about 50 B per building against 982 B), 500 m tiles, LOD2 only within 300 m of the design; (3) BVH for picking and rays; (4) cone parameters as JSON; (5) check and PDF in Workers; (6) service-worker cache; (7) 2D profile fallback without WebGL. Verify on three laptop classes with a fixed benchmark scene, including a thin-and-light and an Apple M-class machine.

modules.name: AI assistance boundaries and verification gates
modules.design_question: What can GPT-6 Astra and Claude do for this node, and where must survey data and people decide?
modules.method: Allowed, always with a human or deterministic check: code, tests and refactoring of Vista modules; data-cleaning and LiDAR-tile scripts; reading PDFs and figures (rezoning booklets, council reports) into candidate table rows; listing the reference buildings named in RTS 16338 Table 2; review of the work of one model by the other; UI copy written from a ViolationReport JSON; fixture generation. Not allowed as a source: terrain, building heights, coordinates, origin elevations, cone parameters or clause text; a reference roof height comes from LiDAR, never from a model. A 2025 study of two LLMs found coordinate offsets and underestimated elevations; Claude documentation calls coordinate outputs approximate. Extraction gate: each model-read number is stored with its page, then must pass (a) recomputation by the City formula where possible, (b) a second-model read, (c) a human check against the page; failures never enter ConeSet. Live data is fetched, not recalled: Astra cutoff is 30 Apr 2026, the Guidelines were amended 4 Feb 2026, open data refreshed 19 Oct 2026. Fetched PDFs and pages are data, not instructions. Check the Buildner AI policy before using AI imagery.

sources.title: HRDEM CanElevation Series (Open Canada)
sources.extract: 1 m or 2 m LiDAR DTM and DSM in the south; CGVD2013; GeoTIFF; Open Government Licence - Canada; modified 2026-05-29; coverage gradual; no accuracy statement.

sources.title: EPSG:3157 NAD83(CSRS) / UTM zone 10N
sources.extract: Area of use: Canada between 126W and 120W (British Columbia); datum NAD83(CSRS) on the GRS 1980 ellipsoid.

sources.title: BC height transformations
sources.extract: HTMVBC00 covers Metro Vancouver, Abbotsford to Hope; HTGVRDBC00 is a related model; both for CGVD28, the current BC vertical datum; ZIP files 26.6-137 KB; no accuracy figures.

sources.title: OpenStreetMap wiki: Key:height
sources.extract: Building height is the maximum from lowest terrain contact to the top including roof; antennas, spires and rooftop equipment excluded; metres by default.

flags.claim: Polygon geometry of each cone is enough to estimate maximum building height at every location.
flags.detail: Dataset has no height fields and its coordinates are 2D (verified). A limit needs a geodetic height per cone, from published site limits, reference-building roofs or the City.
flags.correction: Polygons give plan extent only; limits come from tiers T1a, T1b or T2 (M04) with an estimate flag; ask views@vancouver.ca.

flags.claim: The real lower boundary slopes, so a flat ceiling drifts about 36 m per km for every cone.
flags.detail: Guidelines s.2 p.3 say horizontal lower boundary; RTS 16338 Table 2 ties each lower boundary to a reference roof; the slope came from one 1995-99 sheet for old View 9.1.
flags.correction: Per-cone hypotheses: H0 flat (default) and H1 sloped, fitted with s = 0 allowed; the 36 m per km figure is deleted.

flags.claim: Vista frame distances and bearings are correct: Barclay 4.56 km at 347.3 deg; 828 Cambie at 47.14 deg on the cone A edge.
flags.detail: The frame is 0.20% short east-west and 0.58% short north-south. Its 0.08 m footprint residual checks registration to the same transform, not metric accuracy.
flags.correction: GRS80 geodesic: 1060 Barclay 4,596-4,639 m at 346.90-347.24 deg; cone A sector 43.28-47.02 deg; 828 Cambie 1,704.8 m at 47.031 deg, 0.19 m outside.

flags.claim: The 0.56 s check on 1 M triangles was measured on a desktop CPU.
flags.detail: The i7-14650HX is an Intel HX-series laptop processor; thin-and-light student laptops are slower and unmeasured.
flags.correction: Relabelled as a high-end laptop figure; targets are 1 s high-end and 3 s thin laptops, to be measured.

flags.claim: The City 2004 sheet has 6 rows and all were recomputed exactly.
flags.detail: Slide 32 holds about 15 rows, with two reference elevations (485 and 495 ft) at the same Dr, which may indicate sub-cones.
flags.correction: Six rows recompute exactly (validation cases); rows are 1995-99 history, not current parameters; other rows have blank cells in the extract.

flags.claim: No local high-resolution terrain is confirmed; origin elevations must come from SRTM, HRDEM or LidarBC.
flags.detail: City LiDAR 2022 covers the City and UBC at about 49 pts/m2 (0.081 m at 95%), CGVD28GVRD; the 17 origins lie in 11 tiles, all confirmed present.
flags.correction: LiDAR-2022 is the primary source for origin z, grade and roofs; HRDEM and SRTM serve only the North Shore backdrop.

flags.claim: Footprints-2009 elevations have no stated datum.
flags.detail: The portal describes TOPELEV_M and BASEELEV_M as geodetic metres; the datum itself is still not named.
flags.correction: Record geodetic, likely CGVD28 (unconfirmed); 2009-era and approximate, so a third source in the roof spread.

flags.claim: A far plane of 8 km is enough for the camera rig.
flags.detail: Named subjects lie 12.5-24.6 km from the origins; the Vista observer camera already uses 45,000 m.
flags.correction: Far plane at least 60 km with reversed-Z or log depth; test that every Table 1 subject renders.

flags.claim: SRTM is accurate enough for origin elevations.
flags.detail: USGS gives 16 m linear error at 90% (about 10 m actual), measured to the canopy top; under H1 an origin error can reach the limit 1:1.
flags.correction: Use LiDAR-2022 for origins; keep SRTM only as a distant backdrop fallback.

flags.claim: A single flat study ceiling is a useful stand-in for a cone.
flags.detail: The City model is one horizontal geodetic height per cone or sub-cone, not one ceiling for all cones; some cones may also carry sub-cones or view shadows.
flags.correction: Keep the user ceiling only as a labelled what-if (T0); default to a per-cone limit with its tier.

flags.claim: The polygon apex equals the by-law origin point (Vista).
flags.detail: 16 apexes match 16 origin points and the four QE apexes agree within 0.33 m, but no survey check exists; open-data text for 9.1 and 9.2 names the older origin.

flags.claim: Eye height is 1.6 m.
flags.detail: No City eye height found; a 5 ft 6 in average-person reference (stature, not eye height) appears in a City Q and A snippet. Keep editable and labelled.

flags.claim: Vertical datum of the City geodetic cone heights.
flags.detail: CGVD28 is likely: BC legal surveys use it (LTSA 465C) and LiDAR-2022 is CGVD28GVRD. A search snippet shows CD-1 by-laws define Geodetic Datum as the City reference surface without naming it.

flags.claim: Which Trout Lake geometry (27.1, 27.2) is in force, and which subject each carries.
flags.detail: City report of 2026-06-23 calls 27.1 the existing cone with updates under review. Table 1 (Jul 2024, Jun 2025) gives 27.1 North Shore Mountains, 27.2 Lions; open data and Vista say 27.1 is the Lions.

flags.claim: Whether the open-data apexes for 9.1 and 9.2 match the amended origin.
flags.detail: The Vista extract of the 2026 Table 1 says base of the City Hall stairs; the Jun 2025 Table 1 and open-data descriptions say Walking Figures plaza.

flags.claim: Guidelines clause text, page numbers and rezoning figures.
flags.detail: Text read in Jul 2024 and Jun 2025 copies of unverified provenance; the 2026-02-04 text and rezoning booklets (HTTP 403) were not read; booklet numbers come from search summaries.

flags.claim: One horizontal plane per view describes the City limit.
flags.detail: Table 2 shows lower boundaries shared between views (G1.2, J1.1) and anticipated heights; the 2004 slides mention sub-cones and view shadow. Test piecewise and multi-reference models.

flags.claim: The roof of the named reference building sets the horizontal limit.
flags.detail: Reading of RTS 16338 Table 2 plus s.2 p.3; footprints-2009 puts the 1008 Cambie tower at 102.68 m against 105.71 m published for cone A. LiDAR-2022 test pending.

flags.claim: Vista code and data packs can be reused openly.
flags.detail: None of the four repos has a LICENSE file; the pack derives from a studio-supplied model plus OSM (ODbL); Form Studio omitted the competition model for ownership. Add MIT or Apache; rebuild packs.

flags.claim: Buildner policy on AI-generated images in entries.
flags.detail: The Tall Challenge FAQ lists the question; the answer was not read. Check before using GPT-6 Astra or any generator for entry imagery.

flags.claim: GPT-6 Astra reads images and PDFs reliably.
flags.detail: OpenAI model page lists image input and text output; PDF file input is not stated, though the PDF guide says vision-capable models accept PDFs. Reliability on tables is untested.

flags.claim: Student laptops meet 5 MB, 30 fps and 500 MB targets.
flags.detail: No device survey; the 0.56 s check ran on one HX-series laptop CPU. Test on three laptop classes.

flags.claim: OSM heights are good enough for rooftop views.
flags.detail: OSM height excludes antennas and spires, but the City counts appurtenances; 4,800 of 9,897 studio-model heights are type estimates. LiDAR-2022 roofs replace them where present.

flags.claim: Default plan buffer and uncertainty values.
flags.detail: sigma_origin 5 m, sigma_hdatum 2 m and sigma_footprint 1 m are placeholders; the WGS84 versus NAD83(CSRS) offset is unquantified; LiDAR sigma is 0.081/1.96 assuming normal errors.

flags.claim: Status of view 12.2 (Granville Bridge).
flags.detail: Jul 2024 Table 1 lists 12.2 (Mount Seymour); Jun 2025 Table 1 omits it though clause 3.4.2 still names it; open data has no polygon for it.

change_log: r1: Added City LiDAR 2022 (CGVD28GVRD, 0.081 m at 95%, 11 origin tiles confirmed) as primary source for origin z, grade and roofs; SRTM demoted to backdrop (USGS 16 m at 90%).
r1: Raised the far plane from 8 km to at least 60 km (reversed-Z or log depth); subjects lie 12.5-24.6 km away; the Vista observer far plane is 45,000 m.
r1: Replaced the Vista equirectangular frame with EPSG:3157 or per-cone ENU via GeographicLib (frame error 0.20% and 0.58%, 0.118 deg); regenerated Barclay and 828 Cambie values geodesically.
r1: Replaced the sloped-boundary assumption with H0 flat default and H1 historical, citing Guidelines s.2 p.3 and RTS 16338 Table 2 (reference roofs); deleted the 36 m per km figure.
r1: Hint for flat limits: a 2.05 deg slope adds 164 m over 4.59 km, yet the 2020 Barclay limit is 123.2 m geodetic (unverified); fit with s = 0 allowed.
r1: Added tier T1b (LiDAR roof of the named reference building) with a hypothesis test on 1008 Cambie (102.68 m facet in 2009 against 105.71 m published).
r1: T1a calibration now needs 2 or more sites spanning 30% of cone length, dated after 2024-07-10 or cones absent from Table 2; added OLS prediction variance with covariance.
r1: Re-derived the uncertainty budget with LiDAR sigmas; added plan buffer and near-edge state; zero silent clears and zero plan-edge misses become tests.
r1: Added governing minimum over cones and a ZoningLimit port; the open zoning data has no height field.
r1: Read Guidelines Jul 2024 and Jun 2025 copies from the scratchpad: clauses 3.1.1-3.1.5 print under heading 3.2; citation format fixed; 2026 text and provenance still unverified.
r1: RTS 16338 shows QE views 3.1 and 3.2.4a deleted and 3.2.1-3.2.4 not reshaped in 2024, resolving the QE lower-portion reports.
r1: Trout Lake status confirmed from RTS 19750 (existing cone, updates under review); found a 27.1/27.2 subject mismatch and 12.2 dropped from Table 1 in June 2025.
r1: Replaced the azimuth sector test by polygon containment and clipping (view 28 has five vertices).

r1: Relabelled the 0.56 s benchmark as a high-end HX laptop result and added thin-laptop targets.
r1: City 2004 sheet has about 15 rows; six recomputed and added as hand checks, labelled 1995-99 history; the 485/495 ft split noted as possible sub-cones.
